newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - June 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - June 13.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
KESRI IS ELECTED CONGRESS PARTY CHIEF

Sitaram Kesri was elected Congress party president. He defeated both Sharad Pawar, the party's leader in the lower house of parliament, and Rajesh Pilot, a Working Committee member of the party. This was the first election to the post in the last 20 years. Out of the 7,557 votes, Kesri polled 6,224 votes. Pawar got 882 votes and Pilot 354 votes. Ninety-seven votes were declared invalid. Kesri said his victory was an acknowledgement of his services after taking over from P.V. Narasimha Rao as provisional president in September last year. It also meant the partymen approved of his decision to withdraw support to the Deve Gowda government, he said.
The Economic Times
SWELLING TAX KITTY PROVES RATE SLASH IS RIGHT

Direct tax collections during this April and May touched 10.25 billion rupees. Finance Ministry officials said this showed the experiment of slashing tax rates across the board would not go wrong. Corporation tax collections fell to 9.01 billion rupees as refunds more than offset incoming flows. But an income tax collection of around 19.26 billion rupees compensated for this, resulting in net direct tax collection of 10.25 billion rupees. Ministry sources said indirect tax collections were a cause for concern.
SBI STAFF MEET FINANCE MINISTER ON ROW

The strike by the State Bank of India (SBI) officers in Bombay was near total. The SBI Officers' Association said about 2,500 officers assembled at the SBI central office and held a demonstration to protest against the suspension of three officers on June 10. The suspended officers were charged with procedural lapses in the CRB Capital Markets fiasco. The association threatened that if the suspension orders were not withdrawn, all SBI branches in the Mumbai circle, comprising Maharashtra and Goa states, would go on strike from June 16. In the June 12 strike only SBI officers in five branches went on a flash strike.
HIND LEVER, POND'S, RESERVE BANK REACH ACCORD

Hindustan Lever, Pond's India and the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) have reached an out-of-court settlement on pricing the preferential allotment of shares to Unilever, officials said. The RBI has given its consent to the agreement. Hindustan Lever's (HLL) board had filed the compromise settlement in the High Court on June 7. The final hearing is scheduled for June 16. The price of an HLL share is now fixed at 357 rupees and that of Pond's at 620 rupees for the preferential allotment. This corresponds to the formula based on the average price of the previous six months. These prices conform to the RBI's original condition for the preferential allotment.
SIEMENS MAY TURN JOINT-VENTURE INTO 100 PCT SUBSIDIARY

The government allowed Siemens of Germany to convert its proposed 70:30 joint venture with Siemens India into a 100 percent subsidiary whenever it wished. The Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) recently cleared the proposal to set up the joint venture. It also allowed Siemens India to sell its stake in the new venture to its parent company in the future. Though the proposal was cleared by the FIPB earlier, it was brought to the board again to include this clause. This was a fallout of Siemens India's reluctance to have a permanent commitment in the new venture.
Financial Express
PANEL LIKELY TO SUGGEST MRL-IOC MERGER

A panel will submit its report on the restructuring of Madras Refineries (MRL) in a week. Sources in the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas said one of the suggestions could be a merger between MRL and Indian Oil Corporation (IOC). They also said a merger was sensible as the MRL was a pure refining company whose products were marketed by the IOC. The IOC could, otherwise, become the holding company with at least a 50 percent stake or management control in the MRL. It is impossible for stand-alone refineries to survive once the oil sector is completely deregulated, the sources said.
TENDERING GIVEN THE GO-BY IN TELECOM ALLIANCES

The government has decided to allow all public sector undertakings under the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) to form strategic alliances and joint venture companies without tenders wherever it is necessary for enhancing competitive ability. Under the new procedure, two or more companies can enter into joint ventures without calling for tenders. The licences will be awarded after getting government approval. The decision was taken by the cabinet committee on infrastructure. The Telecoms secretary said the new policy would enable the ministry to expedite the liberalisation of the telecom sector and help India face international competition.
FOREIGN BROADCASTERS HAVE NO CASE TO HIKE STAKE

The information and broadcasting minister said foreign broadcasters lobbying for majority stakes in their Indian joint ventures had no sound basis to press their cases. Foreign broadcasters should be ready for legislation similar to that in their own countries, he said. Most developed countries such as the United States and France do not allow more than 25 percent foreign equity participation in electronic media ventures. The minister hinted at an early implementation of the impending Prasar Bharati Act (Broadcast bill) which has been on the statute book since 1990.
Business Standard
STATE BANK OF INDIA STAFF STRIKE CRIPPLES ITS OPERATIONS

The impasse over the suspension of three State Bank of India (SBI) officers in the CRB Capital Markets case continued for the second day. All SBI officers in the Bombay circle abstained from work in protest. Plans were drawn up by the SBI Officers' Association to deal with the situation. A high-level executive committee meeting of the association is scheduled to be held in Calcutta on June 17. If the deadlock is not broken by then, the issue will be taken up for further discussion and a future course of action will be formulated. Senior officials of the Association have said that the stir will be intensified if the management does not exonerate the officials.
BROKERS TO BE RESPONSIBLE FOR SUB-BROKERS TRADES

Brokers will have to undertake complete responsibility for settlement of trades with sub-brokers under norms finalised by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI). The regulator gave details of the nature, responsibility and regulation of the sub-broking community to the major bourses. A copy of the final modalities was issued late last evening. According to the modalities, the brokers will also be responsible for sorting out pending investor-grievance cases and disputes of the sub-brokers with their clients. Periodical inspection of the sub-brokers accounts and premises will also have to be undertaken.
INDIA OFFERS 7-YEAR SCHEDULE TO PHASE OUT IMPORT CURBS

India has offered to shorten the schedule for phasing out all import curbs from nine years to seven years. But, even this new offer was unacceptable to India's major trading partners, including the United States and the European Union. Diplomatic sources said the Indian delegation had finally backed down and indicated they could consider reducing the transition period to seven years. However, this phase-out period was also rejected by the developed countries, who have been insisting on a two to three year phase out schedule.
NEW BILL TO COVER OFFENCES BY COMPANY DIRECTORS

The finance minister indicated that directors, including government nominees, on the boards of companies will be held responsible for corporate misdemeanour. The finance minister said the bulk of corporate governance should be on the basis of self-regulation. Directors, including government nominees, are not ornaments. Those who do not take their task seriously will have to pay the price of culpability, he said. The minister said the economic reforms that began in 1991 had opened up a host of business opportunities for those who wish to express their entrepreneurial skills as well as those with doubtful entrepreneurial skills.
The Observer
FUND-BUYING PUSHES BOMBAY BOURSE INDEX UP 53 POINTS

The Bombay bourse ended with smart gains on heavy fund buying in front-bencher stocks. The market seems to be shifting to a new range of 3,800 to 4,100 points, said a chief dealer at ASK-Raymond James Securities India. Market action is focused on front line shares, with some second-tier stocks attracting profit-booking by investors and local institutions, players said. Bombay's 30-share index ended 53 points or 1.85 percent higher at 3,980.58. This took the market into a three-day rally, racing 145 points, or nearly four percent, in its winning streak.
FOREIGN INVESTMENT PROMOTION BOARD REJECTS RPG PROPOSAL

The Foreign Investment Promotion Board rejected a proposal for transferring the licence from RPG-SatCom to RPG Telephones. It was rejected because the Department of Telecommunications said it amounted to a change of the Indian partner. RPG's proposal was for allowing RPG Telephones, newly created under the RPG Enterprises, to run V-Sat services. According to the proposal, RPG Communications Holding will hold a 51 percent stake and three Japanese firms will hold a 49 percent foreign stake.
MOVE FOR ANTI-DUMPING DUTY ON NEWSPRINT OPPOSED

The newspaper industry is up in arms against the government's move to levy anti-dumping duty on newsprint imports. They said such moves will hurt the industry, which is reeling under problems like rising input costs and falling advertising revenues. The Indian Newspaper Society is meeting on June 13 to discuss the issue. The designated authority of anti-dumping which is a quasi-judicial organisation in the Commerce Ministry has already recommended that the ministry levy a provisional anti-dumping duty on import of newsprint after conducting an enquiry.
EARLY DECISION ON TELECOM DEPARTMENT CORPORATISATION

The communications minister promised to take a decision on the restructuring and corporatisation of the Department of Telecommunications before year-end. The minister said India was ready for negotiations on the international accounting rate controversy with the U.S. administration. There is a request from the U.S. government and a delegation is scheduled to reach Delhi, he said. The minister refused to set a time limit for the Indian response to the United States' objection to what it considered high international call rates.
